key_insight: EDA-L2D uses recent expert outcomes to adapt when an AI system defers decisions as human reliability changes over time.
clinical_relevance: Adaptive deferral could support medical AI workflows when clinician performance fluctuates, though clinical benefit is not established by the abstract.
method: Model temporal changes in expert reliability.
Condition the deferral head on recent expert outcomes using a sequence model.
Adapt decision allocation between AI and human experts.
evidence_signal: Experiments spanning image classification, medical diagnosis, and hate speech detection report better system performance and deferral decisions than prior L2D methods, including under irregular reliability shifts.
watch_item: Deployment would require timely, reliable feedback on expert outcomes; the abstract does not establish prospective clinical safety.
paper_title: Learning to Defer under Expert Drift
